title: RT Mechanics as Recursive Relational Completion
governing_commitment: Systematic mathematical formalization, internal consistency, intellectual honesty about the provisional nature of all results, welcoming falsification, and presenting individual reasoned perspective rather than empirically validated science.
summary: Defines a provisional induction rule for RT mechanics as recursive relational completion: an unresolved distinction D(*|r) is resolved not by local value assignment but by finding the unique x such that the surrounding relational field achieves admissible closure traceable to the Core Expression. The apparent circularity in 'x is admissible iff it produces RT' is rewritten as mutual constitution through iff_R, mirroring the structure of Axiom 1.2.1 itself. A Trace Inheritance condition is recorded as the open obligation required to validate the recursive engine across nesting depth.

core_insight.label: Mutual Constitution, Not Circularity
core_insight.statement: The condition 'Red_x(F') = RT' is not circular. RT is not a pre-given target that x must hit. RT is the name for the state in which a relational field achieves residue-conditioned closure traceable to RT_core := [(E!=0) iff_R delta_a(E>0)]. This mirrors the structure of Axiom 1.2.1, where constraint (E!=0) and realization (delta_a(E>0)) are mutually constituted through iff_R; neither side is ontologically prior. The admissibility of x and the constitution of RT are co-produced through the same closure relation.
core_insight.textbook_grounding: Axiom 1.2.1 Commentary: neither view (relational nor selection) is prior. The biconditional iff_R carries simultaneous logical, relational, and processual readings. The symmetry/asymmetry duality note states that the form of the axiom enacts the content of the framework.
core_insight.consequence: The correct closure criterion in the induction rule is not '= RT' as a target match, but 'the expression containing D(x|r) is relationally closed under PRIN_001 trace requirements.' RT is then defined as any relational field satisfying those trace requirements. This sidesteps the apparent circularity without changing the substance of the mechanics.

induction_rule.label: RT Mechanics Induction Rule
induction_rule.informal: RT mechanics begins when an unresolved distinction cannot be solved as an isolated value, but can be solved by relational closure.
induction_rule.formal_trigger: D(*|r) appears within a distinction field F such that no local value assignment to * resolves D(*|r) in isolation.

base_case.label: RT Base Case
base_case.admissibility_reading: x=0 is admissible because the field containing D(0|1) satisfies relational closure: the expression can trace its dependency lineage to RT_core without breaking distinction, admissibility, residue closure, or non-collapse (PRIN_001). The base case does not presuppose RT as a target; it constitutes RT through closure verification.
base_case.governance_note: Base case is illustrative. Full constructive trace from D(0|1) to RT_core is a registered proof obligation (see open_obligations below).

general_form.label: General RT Reduction Schema
general_form.find: x such that D(x|g) makes F' := {D(a|b), D(c|d), D(e|f), D(x|g)} relationally closed
general_form.closure_criterion: F' is relationally closed iff every member of F' can constructively trace its dependency lineage to RT_core := [(E!=0) iff_R delta_a(E>0)] without breaking distinction, admissibility, residue closure, or non-collapse (PRIN_001).
general_form.admissibility_principle: x is admissible iff F' (with D(*|g) resolved to D(x|g)) satisfies the closure criterion. RT is then the name for F' in its closed state. Admissibility and RT constitution are co-produced; neither is prior.
general_form.forbidden_reading: x is admissible because it hits RT as an independently specified target. RT is not pre-given; it is constituted by closure.
general_form.compact_form: D(*|r) -> D(x|r) iff F' containing D(x|r) satisfies PRIN_001 closure

stages.description: Distinctions appear in the field F.
Some distinction D(*|r) is unresolved; * admits no local assignment.
The unresolved part cannot be solved alone; it requires the surrounding relational field to constrain admissible candidates for *.
The surrounding field conditions admissible x-values by the PRIN_001 trace requirement: only x-values that allow F' to trace to RT_core without breaking closure are admissible.
The admissible x is selected. D(*|r) -> D(x|r). F' achieves relational closure. This closed F' is what RT names at depth n.
The completed RT_n becomes a new distinction-bearing term: RT_n -> D(RT_n | continuation). This is the recursive engine; closed relational events fold back as left-bearers of new distinctions.

recursive_engine.label: RT Recursive Engine
recursive_engine.reading: A completed RT at depth n is not terminal. It becomes the left-bearer of a new distinction relation, supplying the relational field for the next reduction. RT mechanics is therefore not scalar calculation but recursive relational completion.
recursive_engine.key_property: Each RT_n that feeds into the next level must carry its trace-admissibility forward. The engine is sound only if trace-admissibility propagates across nesting depth.
recursive_engine.open_edge: Trace Inheritance: whether lawful RT_n feeding into D(RT_n | continuation) under the Nesting Coupling Rule (PRIN_003) inherits trace-admissibility into RT_{n+1} without requiring full re-derivation from RT_core. This is the primary open obligation (see below).

mutual_constitution_note.label: Parallel to Core Expression Structure
mutual_constitution_note.statement: The mutual constitution of x-admissibility and RT at each reduction step is structurally parallel to the mutual constitution of (E!=0) and delta_a(E>0) in Axiom 1.2.1. In both cases, iff_R holds not because one side grounds the other, but because they are co-produced through residue-conditioned closure. The RT induction rule enacts the content of the Core Expression at each step of its own recursion.

open_obligations.label: Trace Inheritance Lemma
open_obligations.statement: If RT_n is trace-admissible under PRIN_001 and D(RT_n | continuation) satisfies the Nesting Coupling Rule (PRIN_003) and GOV-RT-ZERO-RECOUPLING-001, then RT_{n+1} := Red_x(D(RT_n | continuation), ...) is trace-admissible without requiring exhaustive re-derivation of the full lineage from RT_core. This would establish that trace-admissibility is a hereditary property under lawful nesting, making the recursive engine formally sound at arbitrary depth.
open_obligations.why_it_matters: Without this lemma, each depth level of the RT engine requires an independent PRIN_001 check from RT_core. With it, the recursive engine is sound by structural induction on nesting depth.
open_obligations.candidate_approach: Show that the PRIN_001 trace requirement is preserved under the Nesting Coupling Rule by demonstrating that the full coupled form [D(*|-*) <f>_x D(*|+*)] at depth n+1 inherits the typed residue structure and asymmetry required by RT_core, via the typed zero-condition structure of Lemma L111.

open_obligations.label: Continuation Admissibility Condition
open_obligations.statement: What constitutes a valid continuation in D(RT_n | continuation)? Without a formal condition on admissible continuations, the recursive engine is open-ended and may admit too much. The continuation term must itself satisfy distinction and admissibility requirements traceable to RT_core.
open_obligations.why_it_matters: An unconstrained continuation space means RT_{n+1} is underdetermined. The continuation condition is the governing constraint that keeps the recursion within the framework's lawful domain.
open_obligations.candidate_approach: Continuation is admissible iff it is itself a member of the distinction domain (E!=0) and can be coupled to RT_n under an asymmetric outer relation from the <*>_x family (PRIN_003). The continuation must carry a typed residue distinguishable from RT_n's residue.

open_obligations.label: Base Case Constructive Trace
open_obligations.statement: Provide a constructive PRIN_001 trace from the base case reduction D(*|1) -> D(0|1) within Red_x(D(0|0), D(0|1), D(1|1), D(0|1)) to RT_core := [(E!=0) iff_R delta_a(E>0)], explicitly showing that distinction, admissibility, residue closure, and non-collapse are preserved throughout.
open_obligations.why_it_matters: The base case is currently asserted rather than constructively traced. This is required before the induction step can be be applied soundly.
open_obligations.candidate_approach: Map D(a|b) notation onto E-values, verify E!=0 at each node of the reduced field, show that delta_a selects x=0 as the unique admissible continuation under the local admissibility window, and confirm residue closure via iff_R.

governance_notes: This induction document has provisional governance status (C1_DEFINED_PROVISIONAL). It may guide hypothesis generation, campaign planning, and further induction target identification, but may not be used for theorem promotion, framework confirmation, or ontology confirmation until open obligations OQ_RTM_001 through OQ_RTM_003 are resolved and independently reviewed.

The mutual constitution claim in core_insight is structurally grounded in Axiom 1.2.1 and its commentary. It does not introduce new axioms; it applies the existing axiomatic structure to the RT mechanics context.
The Trace Inheritance Lemma (OQ_RTM_001) is the highest-priority open obligation. Its resolution would close the formal soundness gap in the recursive engine.
